Heard Sri Vijay M.Malali, learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt. Praveena Y.
Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

2. Petitioner is seeking anticipatory bail in respect of Crime No.74/2024 of respondent Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 423, 341, 504, 506 and 149 of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC").
3.
It is the case of the prosecution that the complainant being a student, was studying in PUC at Rattihalli Government Pre-University College.
She was traveling to her college on everyday.
The petitioner herein being a resident of said Rattihalli was studying ITI at Rattihalli college.
It is stated that he insisted the complainant to love him for the past four years.
She is stated to have developed intimacy with him and exchanged their mobile numbers.
It is further stated that her engagement was fixed with another person.
Having learnt the said fact, the petitioner herein insisted her to accompany him and also assured that he would marry her.
On 17.04.2024, he took her to Hubli and asked the complainant to stay in her friend's house for two days and assured that he would come and marry her in the mosque and went away.

Thereafter,
the complainant asked her parents to come to the place where she was residing and went along with them to her place and narrated the incident to her parents.
On 27.04.2024, her father, maternal uncle went to the house of the petitioner and asked the petitioner to marry the complainant.
However, he has refused to marry the complainant.
The complainant after being cheated by the petitioner, lodged a complaint against him before the jurisdictional police.
The investigation is under progress.
5. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is the innocent of the alleged offences and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The averments of the entire complaint would disclose that both the complainant and the petitioner were loving each other.
However, due to some difference of opinion between them, the petitioner has refused to marry the complainant.
Mere refusal NC: 2024:KHC-D:7971 of marriage cannot be termed as cheating.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for bail.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the petitioner is aged about 21 years and he is a student and also permanent resident of Rattihalli Village, Haveri District.
He will abide the conditions in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

7. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submits that the petitioner and the complainant as per the averments of the complaint were loving each other and he had promised her that he would marry her at Hubli in the mosque.
However, after taking her, he abandoned her in her friend's house and came back to his village.

8. It is further submitted that when the complainant and her parents went to the house of the petitioner to seek for justice, he assaulted and insulted the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7971 complainant and her parents and therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.
9. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the complaint, it appears that the petitioner herein was studying ITI and resident of Rattihalli.
The complainant was studying in the Pre- University College situated at Rattihalli.
They said to have developed intimacy with each other and they have decided to marry each other.
However, her engagement was fixed with another person on 20.04.2024.
The said fact was informed to the petitioner by the complainant.
The petitioner induced her to come out of the house in order to cancel the engagement and he assured that he would marry her.
10. Believing his version, she came out of the house and joined him.
The petitioner took her to Hubbali and asked her to stay in her friend's house and assured that he would return and marry her.
however, he did not marry her.

Being aggrieved by the act of the petitioner, she lodged a NC:
2024:KHC-D:7971 complaint against the petitioner for the above said offences.
However, on perusal of the entire averments of the complaint, the petitioner may be enlarged on bail by imposing conditions without adverting to the merits of the case.

11. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No. 74/2024 of respondent Police Station in the event of their arrest, on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional police and also the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:-
a) The petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional police station within one month from today.
b) The petitioner shall co-operate with the investigation as and when it is required.
